subject: Re: Pricing mechanics for private deployment — node commit / platform-fee offsets
messages:
From: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@medisys.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@medisys.com>, procurement@medisys.com
Date: 2026-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment pricing mechanics — need clarity on offsets

Rachel, thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a clear write-up on how Redwood handles the interplay between node-based commit, platform fee amortization, and support tiers for on-prem/VPC deployments. A few specific asks: 

- If we commit to 12 nodes for 12 months, how do you apply the platform fee? Is it amortized, billed upfront, or can we offset it against node commits?
- Are operator licenses (per-seat) treated separately or included in node pricing?
- What tradeoffs exist if we want a lower platform fee in exchange for a longer commit or higher oncall retainer?

I've attached our draft SOW (Medisys_SOW_v1.pdf) and a simple node-count forecast. Can you advise with an example (12-node commit, 18-month ramp to 36 nodes) and a couple of commercial levers we could use?

Tom
Head of Platform Engineering
Medisys Health
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@medisys.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing mechanics — need clarity on offsets

Tom — thanks for the clear list, and appreciate the SOW. High level answers up front, then I'll follow with a worked example and a proposal for options you can present to procurement.

Short answers:
- Platform fee: normally invoiced as an annual platform fee (can be annualized or invoiced upfront). We frequently amortize it across node commits if the customer signs a multi-year reserved capacity agreement — that yields a lower monthly effective platform charge.
- Operator licenses: sold as an add-on (operator-seat or cluster license). For larger node commits we can bundle a number of operator seats into the node SKU.
- Tradeoffs: lower platform fee can be achieved via longer commits, higher node minimums, or accepting a larger non-refundable implementation credit. Oncall/retainer swaps can substitute part of the platform fee but require a scoped SRE retainer and SLA adjustments.

I'll put numbers into the 12-node/18-month-to-36-node scenario and loop in Jonas for the amortization math. Alex, can you add typical operator-seat banding we use for deals of this size?

Rachel
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing mechanics — need clarity on offsets

Rachel / Alex — preliminary numbers below; assume list prices for this exercise (we can apply negotiated discounts later).

Assumptions:
- Node list: $10k / node / month (licensed throughput-based SKU)
- Platform fee: $120k / year (standard for this tier)
- Operator license: $12k / seat / year
- Implementation credit (one-time): $40k

Scenario: 12 nodes committed, month 1-6 stable at 12, month 7-18 linear ramp to 36 nodes. 18-month term.

Simple approach: amortize platform fee pro-rata across committed node-months. Committed node-months = 12 nodes * 18 months = 216 node-months. Platform fee annual = $120k -> for 18 months = $180k. Per-node-month platform allocation = $180k / 216 = $833.33. Effective per-node-month price = $10,000 + $833.33 = $10,833.33.

Offsets: If Medisys pre-pays platform fee upfront we can offer a prepay discount (5% on platform fee) or we can apply platform fee credit equal to implementation credit for year 1 (e.g., use $40k impl-credit to reduce platform fee). Alternatively, a 36-month commitment allows us to reduce platform fee 10% (economy of scale).

I'll prepare a short two-option commercial that Rachel can send to Medisys: (A) 18-month amortized (baseline), (B) 24-month anchor with platform-fee credit and bundled operator seats.

Jonas
Senior Commercial Ops
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing mechanics — need clarity on offsets

Quick operator-seat guidance for Medisys: for up to 24 nodes we typically include 2 operator seats; for 25-48 nodes we include 4 seats. Additional seats priced at $9k/seat/year on negotiated deals. If they want the operator license bundled fully into the node SKU as a discount, we can decrease node list by 4% and include 3 seats for the 12-to-36-node ramp scenario.

Also flag: if they require air-gapped/on-prem packaging there is usually a packaging surcharge (one-time) — we should confirm their topology vs pure VPC.

Alex
Sales Engineering
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@medisys.com>
Cc: Lisa Moreno <lisa.moreno@medisys.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, procurement@medisys.com
Date: 2026-06-03T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing mechanics for private deployment — sample commercial options

Tom / Lisa — sorry for the delay; attached is a short two-option commercial summary and the node-rate worksheet (private-deploy-ratecard.xlsx). Highlights: 

Option A — 18-month committed path (amortized platform fee)
- Commit: 12 nodes, 18 months
- Platform fee: $180k for 18 months (amortized across 216 node-months) -> ~$833/node-month
- Node price (list): $10k -> effective node-month: $10,833
- Operator seats: 3 included (as Alex suggested, bundled); additional seats $9k/yr
- Implementation credit: $40k applied to year-1 platform fee (reduces platform to $140k)

Option B — 24-month anchor (better economics)
- Commit: 12 nodes, 24 months with ramp to 36 at month 12
- Platform fee: $216k for 24 months (10% discount for 24m) -> amortized per-node-month lower by ~10%
- Node price discount: 4% if operator seats fully bundled into node SKU
- Oncall retainer swap: optional $60k/yr retainer can replace up to 30% of platform fee if they accept a defined SRE scope and extended response SLA

Recommendation: If procurement wants simplicity, go Option A with the $40k impl-credit applied. If they want better unit economics and longer-term predictability, Option B reduces platform and node effective price. Both options include a conversion clause allowing a credit for unused platform fee if they accelerate expansion above committed nodes.

Next steps: Tom, can you confirm whether Medisys prefers prepay vs invoice scheduling, and whether this is VPC-only (no airgap) so we skip packaging surcharge? If procurement wants a formal redlineable term sheet I can have Legal draft a short addendum.

Thanks — Rachel
From: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@medisys.com>

Rachel — this is very helpful, thanks. Procurement prefers an invoice schedule (quarterly) rather than full prepay. Medisys confirmed VPC-only (no airgap) so no packaging surcharge. Two quick asks before we share internally: 

1) Can you show Option A with platform fee reduced by the $40k implementation credit (explicit line items) and the quarterly invoice cadence?
2) For Option B, can you show the math if we instead commit to 36 months (what's the platform fee discount and effective per-node-month)?

If you can send those two small tables and a short paragraph describing the oncall retainer scope for the swap option, we'll put this on the procurement agenda next week.

I'll review the workbook and come back with internal timing.

Tom
